findings.text: the row 'solo runs at head, after the fix' cites five runs whose logs (logs/solo-fix-1.log .. solo-fix-5.log) each record '# revision: a309504070d9bf28cfccafa2077b6c828bb48c43', a commit that predates the faulthandler fixture added in fc2c69052, and none of the five logs contains a 'Timeout (0:01:00)!' dump even though every call runs 138.46-152.69 s against the 60 s interval, while all five base-arm solo logs (solo-run-1..5.log, revision 7034624c1) do dump; those runs therefore neither ran at the landed head nor exercised the dump-adjacent crash the fixture claims to suppress, so the brief's required 'five solo runs at head' arm is absent and the row's label is false.

the summary attributes the crash to a pytest-timeout kill at the 600 s mark, and the node's own logs refute that mechanism: logs/suite-head.log records 'worker gw6 crashed' immediately after the 60 s faulthandler dump in a suite that finished in 269.09 s (so a 600 s mark could not have fired), the two solo deaths are at 75 s and 78 s (logs/solo-run-1.log, logs/solo-run-4.log) which is mid-first-build, and pyproject.toml sets no timeout_method so pytest-timeout's signal method would report a failure rather than a crashed worker; the section 'Where the time goes' records the correct account, so the record's headline contradicts its own body and its own logs.

the comment justifies deleting the determinism assertion 'assert first == cc.build()' by saying a second call 'doubles a cost that already runs to minutes', and the node's logs contradict that: at base the two-build test spends 140.17, 144.70 and 145.61 s in the call, at head the one-build test spends 138.46, 140.59, 147.73 and 149.37 s, so the removed call bought no measurable time and the repository lost its only assertion that build() is deterministic and idempotent for no measured gain.

the retained gate compares the rebuilt document against cascade_thresholds.json, which build() itself reads at imas_codex/standard_names/review/cascade_calibration.py:501 and echoes verbatim at :547 as block['rubric']={dimensions,offset}, so those fields cannot differ by construction, and content_sha256 is recomputed from the compared content on both sides and adds no independence; the assertion does discriminate on the derived cutoffs, route counts and intervals (the reverted operating-point row reddens it, logs/negative-control-final.log, EXIT=1), but the self-referential subset must not be read as covered.

the reviewed run's test_logs names /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261028T114520975730-sib-cascade-calibration-crash/logs/sigsegv-profile-arm.log, which does not exist in that directory, so one of the cited arms cannot be opened or checked by a reader.
